Reference / regex/pattern

regex/pattern#

Okkama Regex Dialect 1 is a locale-independent regular-language dialect implemented by a bounded Thompson NFA.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let date = Regex("(?<year>\\d{4})-(?<month>\\d{2})");
date.found("due 2026-11");                   // true
match date.first(text) {
    case Maybe.some(due) {
        due.int("year");
    }
}
for date.all(text) -> each { ... }           // every match, in order
date.replaced(origin: text, by: "YYYY-MM");  // literal, $ is not expanded
Regex(",\\s*").parts("a, b,,c");             // ["a", "b", "", "c"]

Description#

Okkama Regex Dialect 1 is a locale-independent regular-language dialect implemented by a bounded Thompson NFA. It supports literals, escaping, ., ^, $, character classes, alternation, capturing/non-capturing/named groups and ?, *, +, {m}, {m,} and {m,n} quantifiers. Backreferences, lookaround, conditionals, recursion, subroutine calls and executable constructs are not part of the dialect. Syntax offsets count Unicode scalar values from zero. Compile limits are 4,096 expression scalars, 256 nested groups, 1,024 captures and 16,384 NFA states. Unicode property data is pinned to Unicode 17.0.0. With ignore_case a letter matches every member of its simple case folding class (statuses C and S of CaseFolding.txt, from the toolchain's tables: Unicode 17.0.0 with Rust 1.97), in both directions: K, k and the Kelvin sign U+212A match each other, and dotless ı and dotted İ match only themselves (#550). With ascii as well, only ASCII letters pair.

Construction retains expression and flags and creates only an empty lazy compile state. expression() and flags() never compile. The first metadata or matching action compiles once and memoizes either its program or typed error.

The common questions are asked of the regex itself (#217). Each searches the whole text; FirstRegexMatch, RegexMatches, RegexSubstitution and RegexParts take a range, a limit or a replacement policy.

Regex.first#

The leftmost match, if there is one.

Regex.all#

all(origin is string) is @RegexMatch

Every non-overlapping match from left to right, as RegexMatches walks them: after an empty match the search moves on by one scalar.

Regex.replaced#

replaced(origin is string, by is string) is string

The text with every match replaced by the literal text by. Dollars are not expanded: RegexSubstitution with ExpandedRegexReplacement reads $1 and ${name}.

Regex.parts#

parts(origin is string) is @string

The text between the matches, as RegexParts splits it: empty leading, adjacent and trailing parts stay.
